Container.Name: RustFS
Container.Overview:
RustFS is an S3-compatible object store written in Rust, Apache-2.0, and one of the alternatives people have been looking at since MinIO's open edition stopped moving. This template runs the official image with the two settings it needs on Unraid.
THIS IS A PRE-RELEASE. Every version RustFS has published so far is a release candidate; there has never been a stable 1.0. Do not put data here that exists nowhere else.
Why this template exists: started as it comes, the container does not run on Unraid at all. It runs as its own built-in user id 10001, so on a share owned by nobody:users it cannot write and dies at startup with "Permission denied". This template runs it as 99:100 instead, which fixes it. It also makes the credentials proper fields, because the image otherwise falls back to a built-in default account and says so twice in its own log.
Ports: 9000 is the S3 endpoint every client connects to. 9001 is the built-in web console.
First start: the log ends with the server listening. If you see "Permission denied", the Data folder is not writable by 99:100.
Container.DonateText: If this template helps you, consider buying me a coffee.
Container.Requires: Set an Access Key and Secret Key below. Left empty, RustFS falls back to a built-in default account that is the same in every copy of the image. This is a pre-release: keep a second copy of anything you store here.

Config.Name: S3 API Port
Config.Description: The S3 endpoint every client (rclone, restic, aws-cli, ...) connects to.

Config.Name: Console Port
Config.Description: The built-in web console. This is what WebUI opens.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where the objects live. Must be writable by 99:100, which is what this template runs the container as.

Config.Name: Logs
Config.Description: Log directory. Without it, RustFS falls back to writing its log to standard output, which still works but leaves nothing on disk.

Config.Name: Access Key
Config.Description: The access key your S3 clients use. Leave it empty and RustFS uses its built-in default account, which is identical in every copy of the image.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: The secret key, paired with the access key above. Use a real generated secret (e.g. openssl rand -hex 24), not a short password.

Config.Name: Console CORS Origins
Config.Description: Which origins the web console accepts. The image ships with * (any). Narrow it to your own address if the console is reachable from outside your network.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: How much RustFS writes to its log: error, warn, info, debug or trace.
